text.title: code-review Core Rules
text.summary: Eight testable rules for a high-throughput, high-quality code review pipeline.

rule.statement: PR diff size MUST be under 400 changed lines (excluding generated files, lockfiles, snapshots). Larger PRs require a `large-pr-approved` label and a written rationale.
rule.rationale: Review quality drops sharply above ~400 lines (Cohen-Brown 2010; Cisco study). Splitting forces logical boundaries and faster turnaround.

rule.statement: Reviewers do not start until lint, types, tests, coverage gate, and security scan are all green. The PR template carries the link to the latest CI run.
rule.rationale: Reviewers should not spend cycles flagging issues automated gates catch. Red CI = the PR is not ready for review.

rule.statement: Reviewers focus on correctness (bugs, edge cases) and design (boundaries, naming, abstractions). Style / formatting issues are delegated to ruff / prettier / eslint. Subjective taste is out of scope.
rule.rationale: Style debates produce review-bottleneck. Automating style turns review into actual review.

rule.statement: An agentic pre-review pass (Claude Code / Cursor) runs BEFORE human review and posts a structured comment: (1) risk callouts, (2) test coverage delta, (3) detected anti-patterns. Human reviewer reads the structured comment first.
rule.rationale: Agentic pre-review is cheap and catches 60-70% of low-hanging issues (missing tests, unhandled errors, magic numbers) before a human spends a single minute.

rule.statement: Merge requires (a) all required checks green, (b) one human approval (two for `critical` modules), (c) all conversations resolved. Bots may auto-merge dependency bumps after a clean check run + 2-hour soak.
rule.rationale: Explicit merge policy prevents review-by-thumbs-up and ensures auto-merge stays scoped to safe categories.

rule.statement: When the repository posts CI status checks, the team has agreed the < 400-line PR convention, the lint / type / test / coverage gates exist and human reviewers are available, the pipeline MUST be triggered by the `pull_request` `opened` and `synchronize` events (never run on demand) and MUST emit, before merge, the 02-output-contract record with all five required fields - `pr_lines`, `ci_green`, `approvals`, `conversations_resolved`, `agentic_pre_review_ran` - computed from the CI run and the PR API, never typed in by hand.

rationale.source: GitHub Actions docs - Events that trigger workflows; GitHub REST API - Pulls

rule.rationale: A pipeline that runs only when someone remembers to invoke it records the PRs that were going to be reviewed carefully anyway and none of the rushed ones. Keying the run to the PR events makes a missing record itself a visible failure, and computing the fields from the API is what makes rubber-stamping (fm-06) detectable in audit.

rule.statement: When the preconditions hold but any required field of the record cannot be computed from the inputs - the PR template carries no CI run link, `pr_lines` is not computable because the generated-file / lockfile / snapshot exclusion list is undefined, or the `critical` module list that sets the approval count is missing - the pipeline MUST fail a required status check naming the missing input and MUST NOT emit a record with a defaulted or guessed value (`ci_green: true` without a run link, `approvals: 1` without a named reviewer).

rationale.source: GitHub docs - About status checks; About protected branches

rule.rationale: The schema pins `ci_green` and `agentic_pre_review_ran` to `const: true`, so a record with an assumed value passes validation and hides exactly the case the gate exists to catch. A failed check with a message costs one CI run; a merged PR whose CI never ran costs an incident.

rule.statement: When any Applies-If fails or any Skip-If holds - a solo developer with no human reviewer, a repository that auto-merges trusted bot PRs, or a read-only vendored repository - the methodology MUST NOT be applied; the skip MUST be recorded against the evidence anchor from Prerequisites (PR URL, ticket or commit) naming the failed precondition and the methodology routed to instead (`best-practices-2026` for the constitution rules, `code-coverage` for the gate), and an AI-only review MUST NOT be reported as a completed code review.

rationale.source: Google Engineering Practices - Code Review Developer Guide

rule.rationale: Every Skip-If case has a look-alike artefact - a bot comment, an auto-merge log - that resembles a review. Without the recorded skip, the next audit counts those PRs as reviewed and the missing human reviewer is never noticed.
